Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the last session! South African players are walking out to the middle and taking their respective field positions. Imam-ul-Haq and Abdullah Shafique are the two openers for Pakistan. Kagiso Rabada has the new red cherry in his hand and is raring to go. Let's go...
... DAY 3, SESSION 3 ...

Shan Masood appeared short of ideas, shuffling through various tactics in search of the final two wickets, but Senuran Muthusamy stood firm, frustrating the bowlers with a mix of solid defense and smart scoring. He first found support in Keshav Maharaj, who played a crucial role in the resistance, before the momentum truly shifted when Kagiso Rabada joined him. Rabada counterattacked brilliantly, and the pair added a vital 98 runs for the last wicket before Asif Afridi finally claimed his sixth to end the innings. After spending so long in the field, Pakistan’s batters now face a challenging task, and it will be interesting to see what they consider a defendable total on this tricky surface. Join us in a bit for the final session.

Asif Afridi was the standout performer for Pakistan on debut, breaking that crucial partnership after both Tristan Stubbs and Tony de Zorzi had notched up well-made fifties. He struck again early on Day 3, leaving South Africa reeling at 235/8, still 98 runs ahead. But once the second new ball was taken, things began to unravel for the visitors - runs came freely, and a sloppy phase saw them drop three catches and miss a stumping within just 19 balls. Though Afridi registered an impressive five-wicket haul, support from the other bowlers was lacking on a pitch that kept low and offered sharp turn.

South Africa began their innings with measured caution, assessing the conditions before looking to accelerate, but Shaheen Afridi struck early, removing Ryan Rickelton and injecting life into the fielding side. Skipper Aiden Markram tried to counter with some crisp boundaries but fell just as he was settling in. From there, Tristan Stubbs and Tony de Zorzi steadied the ship brilliantly, stitching together a resilient 113-run stand off 223 balls. Their composed and calculated approach frustrated the bowlers and shifted the momentum, putting South Africa in a strong position while the hosts searched desperately for a breakthrough.

With that, it is TEA ON DAY 3! SESSION SUMMARY - 119 runs and 2 wickets in 25.3 overs! We’ve witnessed a remarkable fightback from South Africa, who not only closed in on Pakistan’s total but surged past it to take a lead of 71 runs. The turnaround was powered by a superb innings from Senuran Muthusamy, who expertly guided the lower order, scoring 89, while Kagiso Rabada produced a stunning counterattack, smashing his way to a career-best 71 and leaving the hosts thoroughly frustrated.

OUT! IN THE AIR... TAKEN! Asif Afridi gets his sixth wicket and the Proteas are all out! Afridi bowls it fuller, pitching it on off and turning it in. Kagiso Rabada looks to slog it away but fails to get underneath the delivery. The ball loops and flies toward the fielder in the long on region. It's Abdullah Shafique, who misjudges the ball at first but eventually does well to lean forward and take the catch near his shoelaces. South Africa ends up with a lead of 71 runs.

This burgeoning partnership might prove to be lethal for Pakistan. Therefore, their aim would be to find the breakthrough and bowl out South Africa as quickly as possible, as the cracks are starting to open on the pitch. It would be interesting to see how Keshav Maharaj's deliveries will grip and turn on this track, as he picked seven wickets on a wicket that was inclined toward the batters. But today, after witnessing the first two hours of play, we can say that the ball is turning a lot, compared to Day 1. Join us for the second session, which is set to commence at 7.40 am GMT.

Senuran Muthusamy and Keshav Maharaj have injected a bit of aggressive intent into their innings, displaying fearless stroke play and effectively finding the boundaries. There have been a couple of critical moments where Pakistan could have seized the opportunity to claim their ninth wicket, but fortune appears to be in favour of the Proteas. The duo has forged a solid partnership, 50 runs in 56 deliveries, and Muthusamy is close to his second Test half-century, sitting just two runs away.

SESSION SUMMARY - 100 runs and 4 wickets in 29 overs. It has been a mixed bag session for Pakistan. They started well, and credit goes to one man, and that's Asif Afridi. By expertly neutralizing a significant threat, he delivered a crucial blow by claiming the wicket of Tristan Stubbs, who had settled in with a formidable 76 runs off 205 deliveries. His dismissal was crucial, as it disrupted the momentum and neutralized the threat that was looming over Pakistan. He also picked up his much-deserved FIVE-FER and now South Africa are eight wickets down. However, things started to go south once they opted for the second new ball as runs started to flow for the visitors.

Commentary.Commentary: All set for Day 3's action to begin. Pakistan players are seen in a huddle, near the fence, before they take their respective fielding positions. Kyle Verreynne and Tristan Stubbs will resume their partnership. Asif Afridi will bowl the first over on Day 3. Here we go...

Tony de Zorzi is in for a chat. He says that he is enjoying the game, focusing on one ball at a time. Continues that their hard work in preparation is paying off, and he's trying to keep things simple by trusting his instincts and backing his defense. Adds that the pitch has been turning from Day 1, and it was a good day for batting first. Reckons that as the day progresses, the pitch will deteriorate further. Ends up saying that he's hopeful, Kyle Verreynne and Stubbs can build a big partnership today

PITCH REPORT - Bazid Khan is near the deck with his insights. He says that the pitch has developed few cracks, not like we all expected, but it's much better than the first day. Adds that rough has developed close to the batters, but it won't be much problem for them, but the spinners might get some points from it. Ends up saying that the heavy rollers haven't been used yet, as it either roughs the pitch or makes it good for batting, so both teams are reluctant to use it.

South Africa, meanwhile, will need to re-strategize. Tristan Stubbs and Tony de Zorzi stitched a useful stand to steady the ship, but after the latter's dismissal, things are not looking great for the visitors. South Africa’s strategy will likely revolve around extending this partnership between Stubbs and Kyle Verreynne, and avoiding any further collapses, cause they only have Marco Jansen left as an all-rounder, but after him, all are tail-enders. If they can eke out another 130-140 runs, they might unsettle Pakistan’s plans, but the onus is firmly on them to shift the momentum. With the Proteas losing four of their batters, will they be able to make a lead on their first inning? Or, will the hosts keep mounting the pressure? Let's find out together!

Yesterday was much positive day for Pakistan. After being bowled out for 333 in the first innings courtesy of a searing seven-wicket haul from South Africa’s Keshav Maharaj, Pakistan responded by holding South Africa to 185 for 4 at Stumps on Day 2, trailing by 148 runs. Tristan Stubbs has proved to be a hurdle for the home side with a patient 68 and still out there, but Pakistan's debutant Asif Afridi will look forward to handle the situation, as he was sensational in the last session of Day 2. Pakistan will therefore look to make early inroads, tighten the screws through their spin battery and seam options, and try to wrap up things quickly to keep a significant lead before they bat again.

Welcome to Day 3 or as we often say the Moving Day of Test cricket, where things get clearer in a particular match. After analysing the first two days, we can say that Pakistan are comfortably holding the upper hand so far, and South Africa are facing the uphill task of mining their way back into the contest. The momentum is with the hosts, but a sturdy partnership from the Proteas could make all the difference in this brand new day.
... DAY 3, FIRST SESSION ...

South Africa still trail Pakistan by 148 runs and with this duo of Tristan Stubbs and Kyle Verreynne being the last proper batting duo, they will have their work cut out in the first session on Day 3. Pakistan will be eager to get atleast a couple of early breakthroughs on Day 3 to gain complete control of this first innings but one big partnership could really make this a close contest. Day 3 will begin on Wednesday, 22nd October at 5 am GMT, but you can join us sooner for the build-up as well. Cheers!

The final session was all about holding fort for South Africa as Tony de Zorzi and Tristan Stubbs continued to frustrate the Pakistani spinners. However, for a long period of time, the scoring rate was very slow. Stubbs and de Zorzi did manage to muster up runs at a much better pace and brought up their individual fifties as well. With things looking pretty even-stevens, debutant Asif Afridi got the breakthrough and soon enough, he got the destructive Dewald Brevis for a duck as well and once again, South Africa were pegged back, leaving Stubbs with all the burden on his shoulders.

South Africa came out to bat just a few minutes before Lunch and managed to negotiate that tricky phase of play, but when conditions were pretty much excellent for batting in the second session, they couldn't quite score at a brisk pace. Aiden Markram did manage to turn on the heat but he perished and the Proteas had to rebuild once again. Shaheen Afridi had laid a good foundation for the spinners and it was Sajid Khan who struck gold in his very first over, dismissing the Proteas skipper, handing the hosts the advantage at that point.

The day started with Pakistan needing a partnership to get back on track and they did get it thanks to a solid stand between Saud Shakeel and Salman Agha. However, the Proteas answered back in the first session itself and Keshav Maharaj ran through the Pakistani middle and lower order, ending up with a seven-wicket haul, but the hosts did manage to get 333 solid runs on the board.

The end of a vital day's play of Test cricket and at the end of Day 2, hosts Pakistan hold the upper hand. South Africa are playing an extra bowler this match, which means Marco Jansen, who is scheduled to come in next, is their all-rounder, and then the tail will follow and they still trail by 148 big runs.

Following the fall of the first wicket, Proteas skipper Aiden Markram quickly shifted gears, confidently capitalizing on any loose deliveries. His momentum, however, was halted when Sajid Khan made an immediate impact, striking in his very first over. Meanwhile, Tristan Stubbs and Tony de Zorzi have settled comfortably at the crease, taking their time to build a sturdy partnership. Pakistan, having lost two of their reviews, now find themselves with just one remaining for the rest of the innings. The urgency to break this partnership is palpable for Pakistan, as allowing these two batters to remain at the crease could spell trouble for the bowlers, as these were the two batters who knocked hefty runs for the Proteas in the previous Test match-up. Join us back around 10 am GMT for the final session on Day 2!

SESSION SUMMARY - 31 overs, 77 runs, and 2 wickets. The track has clearly opened up for the spinners, with deliveries gripping and turning significantly more than on the first day. The tourists started the session cautiously, assessing how the ball behaves on this surface. However, Shaheen Afridi struck gold by securing the vital opening breakthrough, setting the tone in favor of the hosts.

Saud Shakeel and Salman Agha did well enough to take Pakistan not just past the 300-run mark but a few runs clear of it as well, but they will feel they have left some runs out there. Shaheen Afridi will be key with the new ball but as the day goes on, the spinners will play a big role. The challenge for South Africa will be to see off the new ball, so that they have set batters at the crease when the spinners really start to come into play from both ends. All in all, a fascinating session awaits, so do join us at 7.40 am GMT for the post-Lunch session on Day 2.

Pakistan walked into Day 2 needing a partnership to steady the ship and after a bit of a wobbly start, Saud Shakeel and Salman Agha managed to forge together a telling stand. The duo mustered up quick runs in the second half of the session and Salman was clearly the enforcer. South Africa were always sniffing a wicket which wasn't coming but they kept Keshav Maharaj going from one end and once he got rid of Salman, the floodgates opened. A stellar seven-wicket haul for the left-arm spinner, a very rare feat to achieve as well.

Aiden Markram and South Africa survive a late barrage in the first session and we have all to play for heading into Lunch on Day 2. The Proteas faced just 3 overs before Lunch and in the final over, Shaheen Afridi did really ask some questions of Markram, but he has managed to survive for now. It will be interesting to see how the pitch plays in the next session after getting baked in the Sun.
